title: Fairness in Large Language Models: A Taxonomic Survey
explain_beginner: Large language models are powerful AI systems, but they can unfairly discriminate against certain groups of people, especially marginalized communities. This paper surveys what fairness means for these systems, how to measure when they're behaving unfairly, and what methods can make them fairer. It also catalogs practical tools and datasets researchers can use to test whether their models treat everyone equally.
explain_business: Deploying language models without fairness safeguards risks legal liability, reputational damage, and customer harm through discriminatory outputs. This reference consolidates evaluation metrics, testing tools, and proven techniques for identifying and reducing bias. Executives can use it to understand what fairness means operationally, what resources exist to audit models, and what remediation strategies are available before deployment.
explain_practitioner: This survey synthesizes current work on fairness in large language models, covering bias sources, fairness definitions specific to LLMs, evaluation metrics, and mitigation algorithms. It catalogs available toolkits and datasets for bias assessment, distinguishing fairness challenges in LLMs from traditional machine learning contexts. The work provides a structured taxonomy of existing approaches and identifies open problems to guide development of fair LLM systems.
